en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Chapter on Simile-Questions, The Lion Section.
1. The Question on the Lion’s Limbs “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘seven limbs of the lion should be adopted,’ which are those seven limbs that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, the one called a lion is white, stainless, pure, and bright;”
In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga, the yogāvacara, must have a mind that is white, stainless, pure, and bright, and be free from remorse.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the lion that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the lion has four feet and moves with a majestic stride.
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga should possess the four bases of psychic power as his feet.
This, Great King, is the second quality of the lion that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the lion has beautiful and splendid manes.
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga must be one who possesses the beautiful and lovely mane of virtue.
This, Great King, is the third quality of the lion that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, even at the end of his life, the lion does not bow down to anyone.
In the same way, Great King, even when his robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick are exhausted, the practitioner of yoga should not bow down to anyone.
This, Great King, is the fourth quality of the lion that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the lion eats in regular succession; in whatever place he falls upon, there he eats as much as he needs, and does not search for choice meat.
In the same way, great king, a practitioner of yoga who is devoted to yoga should be one who eats from house to house;
he should not select families, nor should he approach families after bypassing his former home;
he should not select his food, but wherever a morsel is taken, there it should be eaten for the sake of sustaining the body. He should not...
Excellent food must be sought out.
This, Great King, is the fifth quality of the lion that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the lion does not eat from hoarded stores; having eaten its prey once, it does not return to it again.
"In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga, a follower of yoga, should be one who does not consume stored-up food.
This, Great King, is the sixth quality of the lion that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, when a lion does not find food, he does not become anxious; and even when he finds food, he consumes it without attachment, without infatuation, and without clinging."
In the same way, great king, a practitioner engaged in yoga, having not obtained food, should not be distressed;
and even when food is obtained, it should be consumed without attachment, without infatuation, without clinging, seeing the danger in it, and possessing the wisdom of escape.
This, great king, is the seventh quality to be adopted from the lion.
This was also spoken, Great King, by the Blessed One, the God above gods, while praising the Elder Mahākassapa in the noble Saṃyutta Nikāya:
“Bhikkhus, this Kassapa is content with whatever almsfood he receives; he speaks in praise of being content with whatever almsfood he receives.
He does not, for the sake of almsfood, engage in improper search, nor does he become dejected when he does not receive almsfood.”

“He does not become agitated; and having obtained almsfood, he consumes it without being attached, infatuated, or clinging to it, seeing the danger in it and possessing wisdom regarding the escape from it.
Thus ends the first question on the lion’s posture.
